## NetCDF output: per-block files and the combine (`outputs: type: netcdf`) {#sec-ch14-netcdf}

### Summary

Output block `<n>` of the card (counting from 0) is stream `out<n>`. Block `<r>` writes frame `<kkkkk>` of that
stream to `<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`. The combined file is `<basename>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`. Every rank returns
from the write only after the combined file exists.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Writes each block's part of an output frame to its own NetCDF-4 file, then joins them into one.

**Data.** Reads the selected variables of the block; writes `<basename>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`.

**Placement.** `make_outputs` after an accepted step; the root joins the parts with the in-tree `mppnccombine`.

**Activation.** `outputs: - type: netcdf` with `dt`, `variables`[^rg-9edf1a86e51f] and options; CMake `NETCDF` (default ON).

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact copy, then float32 unless `double_precision`[^rg-60f001cddf89]: at most $2^{-24}$ relative.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-netcdf-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $f$ a cubed-sphere panel, $0..5$ [count]; $n_{b2}$, $n_{b3}$ the
blocks per panel along $x_2$, $x_3$ [count]; $\mathrm{fl}_{32}(x)$ the float32 value nearest a double $x$; $t$ the
written time [s].

### Derivation

The output copies values and, by default, rounds them to float32. What that rounding costs, in four steps:

1. *The conversion.* Each value is converted with `static_cast<float>` into an `NC_FLOAT` buffer unless
   `double_precision: true` ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}}). The cast rounds to
   nearest.
2. *Relative error.* For $\lvert x\rvert$ in the float32 normal range $[2^{-126},\,(2-2^{-23})\,2^{127}]$, rounding to the
   nearest of 24 significant bits gives $\lvert\mathrm{fl}_{32}(x)-x\rvert\le 2^{-24}\lvert x\rvert\approx5.96\times10^{-8}\lvert x\rvert$.
3. *Outside that range.* A value above $\approx3.40\times10^{38}$ becomes infinite. One below $2^{-126}$ goes
   subnormal, with absolute error at most $2^{-150}$.
4. *The time.* The time is written in the same type. Near $t$ the float32 spacing lies between $2^{-24}t$ and
   $2^{-23}t$, so a step shorter than $2^{-25}t$ always vanishes from the written time and one longer than
   $2^{-23}t$ always shows. This is the "time step below about $10^{-7}t$" of the code comment.

With `double_precision: true` the file holds the doubles exactly. `[C17]`–`[C19]` of `derivation_check.py` check
steps 2 to 4.

### Numerical method

**Options.** `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml` accepts only the keys listed above plus `data_format` and `verbose`; it
rejects a slice and a sum along the same axis and requires `type`[^rg-ddd3dfc3359d]
({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The defaults are where `OutputOptionsImpl` declares each option with `ADD_ARG`
({{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl >}}).

**One block's file.** `NetcdfOutput::write_output_file` does nothing on the final write, so the last frame of a run is
the last scheduled one (@sec-ch14-schedule). It writes the interior, or with `include_ghost_zones` the interior plus
$n_g$[^rg-88a9e0a977ff] ghosts on every axis with more than one cell. It applies slices and sums, then creates the file with
`nc_create(..., NC_NETCDF4, ...)` ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}}). Each block records its
position in the global block grid. For the cubed sphere the six panels are laid out as a $3 \times 2$ tile: panel $f$
is shifted by $(f \bmod 3)\,n_{b2}$ in $x_2$ and $\lfloor f/3 \rfloor\,n_{b3}$ in $x_3$, and the global counts become
$3n_{b2}$ and $2n_{b3}$ (`nb2`, {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}}). Every variable, the time
included, is NC_FLOAT unless `double_precision: true`, which makes it NC_DOUBLE
({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}}).

**The combine.** `combine_blocks` counts the blocks of the process that have written this frame. Only the last of
them goes on, so one thread per process enters the collective part (`ready_to_combine`, {{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp ready_to_combine >}}).
That thread waits at a barrier. It then creates a scope guard whose destructor is a second barrier, so no rank
returns before the root has finished, and a throw on the root still releases the others. On the root it globs
`<basename>.block*.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc` and removes any old combined file. One part is renamed; several parts are passed
to `mppnccombine -r`, which joins them and removes the parts (`ReleaseOnExit`, {{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::combine_blocks >}}).
`mppnccombine` is GFDL's tool for joining decomposed NetCDF files, compiled in as a function
({{< code src/output/mppnccombine.cpp mppnccombine >}}).

With `combine: false` the per-block files stay. Joining them later needs an external `mppnccombine`;
`pd-combine` does not join blocks (@sec-ch14-tools).

#### What is in the file

**Which writers exist.**

A first-year reading: every entry of the `outputs:` list in the YAML card is one *stream*. Its `type:` picks the writer.

: Netcdf contract, table 2. {#tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-2}

**Inside a NetCDF file: names, units, prognostic or diagnostic.**

Two state arrays sit behind the names:

- `hydro_w` is the *primitive* state: total density $\rho$[^rg-bc477a8d0f7b], velocities, pressure, and mass fractions $y$.
- `hydro_u` is the *conserved* (prognostic) state: dry density (for `ideal-moist`), partial densities $\rho y$, momenta, total energy.

| id | fact | source |
|---|---|---|
| O-16 | Row order of both arrays in the default build (`NMASS` = 0): 0 density, 1-3 velocity or momentum, 4 pressure or energy, 5 onward species | [parameters.cmake#L3](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/cmake/parameters.cmake#L3), [snap.h#L34-L41](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/snap.h#L34-L41) |
| O-17 | In `hydro_u`, row 0 is the **dry** density $(1-\sum y)\rho$, the species rows are partial densities $y\rho$, and the momentum is $\rho v$ (lowered with the cell cosine). In `hydro_w`, row 0 is the **total** density $\rho$ and the species rows are mass fractions $y$ (shown for `ideal-moist`) | [ideal_moist.cpp#L140-L152](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/eos/ideal_moist.cpp#L140-L152) |

: Netcdf contract, table 5. {#tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-5}

Watch-outs for a reader of the files:

- The pressure unit string is lower-case "pa" (O-18).
- Mass fractions, partial densities, `dens`, `Etot` and `mom*` carry no `units` attribute at all (O-18, O-19). Their SI[^rg-8c117ccbf00d] units are not stated in any output code.
- **Hypothesis, not run:** `variables: [prim, cons]` on a deck with species defines each species name twice: once from `hydro_w`, once from `hydro_u` ([load_hydro_output_data.cpp#L155-L161](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/output/load_hydro_output_data.cpp#L155-L161)). `nc_def_var` is wrapped in a check that throws on error ([netcdf.cpp#L325-L348](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/output/netcdf.cpp#L325-L348)), so a "name in use" write failure is expected. This hypothesis has not been run.

**Dimensions, coordinates and ghost cells in NetCDF.**

| id | fact | source |

: Netcdf contract, table 6. {#tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-6}

Cadence is described in @sec-ch14-schedule. The existing ghost-zone limits above still apply.

### Code

**A minimal input.** One NetCDF stream of the primitives and two diagnostics every 100 s, in double precision:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `outputs`[^rg-b5340f5bdc7f].
```yaml
outputs:
  - type: netcdf
    variables: [prim, uov]
    dt: 100.            # s; 0 writes every cycle
    double_precision: true
```

**What is refused, and why.** `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` reads the `outputs` list one entry at a time
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), and `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
parses each entry ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). In order:

1. *An unknown key* in the entry is an error (`check_keys` with the accepted keys), so a misspelt option is not
   silently dropped.
2. *A slice and a sum along the same axis* ("Cannot request both slice and sum along x1") is an error. One axis
   cannot be both cut and summed.
3. *A missing `type`* is an error ("output file type must be specified"). There is no default writer.
4. *A slice outside the mesh* is an error ("Slice at x1=… is out of range of Mesh"), checked against the global
   bounds.
5. *An unknown `type`* is an error when the block builds its outputs ("Output type '…' is not implemented"); `pnetcdf`
   without `PNETCDF=ON` is refused there too.

**The excerpt.** The precision switch of step 1, in `NetcdfOutput::write_output_file`:

```cpp
const bool nc_dbl = options->double_precision();
const nc_type nctype = nc_dbl ? NC_DOUBLE : NC_FLOAT;
...
f[i] = static_cast<float>(v);      // fl32(x) of step 2 when nc_dbl is false
```

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| option defaults | {{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl >}} | `ADD_ARG` | none |
| options from YAML | {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml` | `outputs` |
| stream name | {{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl::file_id >}} | `file_id` | none |
| one block's file | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}} | `NetcdfOutput::write_output_file` | `include_ghost_zones` |
| cubed-sphere tile | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}} | `nb2` | `layout: cubed-sphere` |
| float or double | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}} | `nc_dbl` | `double_precision` |
| last block of the process | {{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp ready_to_combine >}} | `ready_to_combine` | none |
| barriers and the combine | {{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::combine_blocks >}} | `NetcdfOutput::combine_blocks` | `combine` |

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_user_output` `OutputPrecision` (double) | values written with `double_precision` read back bit for bit | exact | NC_DOUBLE |
| `test_user_output` `OutputPrecision` (non-finite) | a non-finite value (an infinity) survives the float output | exact class | IEEE |
| `test_user_output` `OutputPrecision` (default) | default off; reported by the options printout | exact | string compare |
| `test_user_output` `OutputSlice.*`, `OutputSelection.*`, `OutputStatistics.*`, `SuperResolution.*` | slices, selections, statistics (@sec-ch14-schedule) and refined output | per case | the test cases |
| `test_output_barrier` | two ranks, two blocks each: on return every rank opens the combined file, which holds every global cell with its value | exact | file contents |
| `test_netcdf_utils` | variable names are sanitised to NetCDF rules | exact | string compare |

`[C17]` of `derivation_check.py`: on $2\times10^5$ random normal-range doubles the largest relative error of the cast is
$5.948\times10^{-8}\le2^{-24}$. `[C18]`: a value above the float32 maximum becomes infinite. `[C19]`: on
$2\times10^4$ float32-exact times, a step below $2^{-25}t$ vanishes and one above $2^{-23}t$ shows.[^ch14-netcdf-chk]

    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch14/derivation_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process;
    Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0; output identical to the committed file]. Output `derivation_check.out`, lines `[C17]`–`[C19]`.

The precision cases are the `OutputPrecision` tests in {{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp >}} (`yaml_double_precision_defaults_off_and_is_reported`,
`netcdf_float_output_keeps_nonfinite`, `netcdf_double_precision_reads_back_exactly`); the barrier case is
`combined_output_is_complete_when_every_rank_returns`
({{< code tests/test_output_barrier.cpp Mesh.combined_output_is_complete_when_every_rank_returns >}}). Pass status at the pin was not run for
this chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The default float output hides relative changes below about $10^{-7}$. Conservation is read from the
  double-precision cycle line, not from the files.
- `include_ghost_zones` carries a FIXME: it "probably doesn't work with grids other than CCC"
  (`FIXME`, {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfOutput::write_output_file >}}).
- The root globs every `block*` part of the frame in the output directory. Parts left over from an earlier run
  with more blocks would be joined in. This is read from the code and has not been run.
- The error path of the scope guard (a throw on the root) is not covered by a test.
:::
